# Compiler Principles {.unnumbered}

Part V treats the policy compiler: the optimization feedback loop that compiles empirical trajectory execution traces back into foundation model weights. Base foundation models possess broad world knowledge but lack reliable agency. We formalize the autonomous data flywheel for mining production execution traces, develop supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with observation loss masking to enforce action invariants, and design reinforcement learning pipelines with verifiable rewards (RLVR / GRPO) grounded in deterministic test suites and compiler oracles.

::: {#pri-vol3-trajectory-post-training .callout-principle title="Trajectory-level post-training"}

**Invariant**: Foundation models cannot reliably act as agents without post-training on multi-turn trajectories containing explicit scratchpad thoughts, tool invocations, and error-recovery paths.

**Implication**: Data curation pipelines must synthesize, filter, and reject-sample multi-turn rollouts through external execution validation to prevent compounding covariate drift.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-action-masked-loss .callout-principle title="Observation loss masking"}

**Invariant**: In multi-turn agent training, optimizing the model to predict external environment responses degrades policy quality and causes hallucinated tool outputs.

**Implication**: The policy compiler must strictly mask the cross-entropy loss over environment observations, computing gradients exclusively on the agent's internal thoughts and action tokens.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-verifiable-rewards .callout-principle title="Reinforcement learning via verifiable feedback"}

**Invariant**: Long-horizon agentic reliability requires optimizing policies against objective, deterministic verification oracles (test suites, linters, schemas) rather than subjective human preference models.

**Implication**: RLVR and GRPO leverage algorithmic reward environments to incentivize self-correction, rigorous verification steps, and deliberate backtracking.

:::
